definitions.explanation: An immeasurably long span of time, or something that lasts forever. Originally a Buddhist term referring to the infinite past or future, now used more broadly in literary and formal contexts.

examples.japanese: {久遠|くおん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{時|とき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{超|こ}える→超える：01942_koeru⟧。
{久遠|くおん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{平和|へいわ}→平和：01507_heiwa⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{願|ねが}う→願う：02387_negau⟧{碑|ひ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{建|た}てられた→建てる：01189_tateru⟧。
examples.english: A monument was erected wishing for eternal peace.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{寺|てら}→寺：01676_tera⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{久遠|くおん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{歴史|れきし}→歴史：02267_rekishi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持|も}ち→持つ：00478_motsu⟧、{何世紀|なんせいき}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧わたって⟦{人々|ひとびと}→人々：03141_hitobito⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{信仰|しんこう}→信仰：03685_shinkou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{集|あつ}めて→集める：01170_atsumeru⟧きた。
examples.english: This temple has an eternal history and has drawn the faith of people for many centuries.

notes:
Composed of {久|く} (long time) and {遠|おん} (distant). Originally a Buddhist term ({久遠|くおん}{実成|じつじょう} refers to the Buddha's eternal existence), it has expanded into literary and formal Japanese.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {久遠|くおん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{時|とき} (eternal time)
- {久遠|くおん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{平和|へいわ}→平和：01507_heiwa⟧ (everlasting peace)
- {久遠|くおん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{歴史|れきし}→歴史：02267_rekishi⟧ (eternal history)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {久遠|くおん}: eternity (literary, Buddhist origin)
- ⟦{永遠|えいえん}→永遠：01873_eien⟧: eternity, forever (most common everyday word)
- ⟦{永久|えいきゅう}→永久：01875_eikyuu⟧: permanence, perpetuity (formal, often in compounds)
